name: Example: Determining Whether a Set of Functions is Orthogonal With Respect to a Given Inner Product
problem:
Consider the following set of functions:

$$
f_1(t)=1, \qquad
f_2(t)=t, \qquad
f_3(t)=2t+1
$$

Given that the inner product in the vector space $\mathcal{C}[-1,1]$ of continuous functions over $[-1,1]$ is defined as 

$$
\langle f(t),g(t) \rangle = \int_{-1}^{1} f(t)g(t) \: \text{d}t,
$$

which of the following statements are true?

- $f_1(t) \perp f_3(t)$ with respect to the given inner product

- $f_2(t) \perp f_3(t)$ with respect to the given inner product

- $S=\{ f_1(t), f_2(t), f_3(t) \}$ is an orthogonal set with respect to the given inner product
worked_solution:
Recall that a set of vectors in an inner product space is called orthogonal if all vectors in the set are mutually orthogonal with respect to the given inner product. 

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

- Statement I is false. We have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨{f}_{1}(t),{f}_{3}(t)⟩ & =⟨1,2t+1⟩ \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}(2t+1)\,\text{d}t \\  & =({t}^{2}+t){|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & ={1}^{2}+1-((-1)^{2}+(-1)) \\  & =2\ne 0.\end{aligned}
$$

This means that $f_1(t) \not\perp f_2(t)$ with respect to the given inner product.

- Statement II is false. We have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨{f}_{2}(t),{f}_{3}(t)⟩ & =⟨t,2t+1⟩ \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}t(2t+1)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}(2{t}^{2}+t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{2{t}^{3}}{3}+\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}{|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =\frac{2(1)^{3}}{3}+\frac{{1}^{2}}{2}-(\frac{2(-1)^{3}}{3}+\frac{(-1)^{2}}{2}) \\  & =\frac{7}{6}+\frac{1}{6} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}\ne 0.\end{aligned}
$$

This means that $f_2(t) \not\perp f_3(t)$ with respect to the given inner product.

- Statement III is false. Since $f_1(t) \not\perp f_2(t),$ the set $S$ is *not* orthogonal.

Therefore, the correct answer is "None of the statements are true."
